title: Why do some countries move their clocks in summer?
examples: Why do clocks go forward in spring?
Does daylight saving give more daylight?
Why doesn't India change its clocks?

explain.say: Did you know that in some countries everyone moves their clocks forward one hour each spring? Look at the curve on the board. It shows the hours of daylight through the year in London. See how it climbs to a peak in June?

draw.text: Why do some countries move their clocks in summer?

explain.say: Look at the left of the graph. In winter, London gets only about 8 hours of daylight, but in June it gets over 16 hours! Far from the equator, summer and winter days are very different. Are winter days short where you live?

See the mark where the clocks go forward? In late March, people in Britain, much of Europe and North America move their clocks one hour ahead. This is called daylight saving time, or summer time. In late October, at the last mark, the clocks go back.

Look at the two sides, for London in June. Summer time doesn't make more daylight. It moves one hour of light from very early morning, when most people sleep, to the evening, when you can play outside. Which side would you pick?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Same daylight, one hour moved to the evening

explain.say: Great thinking! Near the equator, in countries like India, Indonesia and Nigeria, days stay close to 12 hours all year, so there's no reason to change clocks. Some people say the switch upsets sleep, so a few countries have stopped it. Should clocks change? What do you think?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Same daylight, one hour moved to the evening

faq.a: Moving the clocks forward one hour in spring and back in autumn, so summer evenings stay light for longer. In Britain it is called British Summer Time.

faq.q: Does changing the clocks give us more daylight?
faq.a: No. The amount of daylight is the same. Changing the clocks only moves one hour of it from early morning to the evening.
asks: Do we get an extra hour of sun?

faq.q: Why don't countries near the equator change their clocks?
faq.a: Near the equator, day and night stay close to 12 hours each all year. There is no long summer evening to save.
asks: Why doesn't India have daylight saving?

faq.a: Germany and Austria-Hungary began it in 1916, during the First World War, to save fuel for lighting. Britain followed a few weeks later.

faq.q: Is changing the clocks good or bad?
faq.a: People disagree. Supporters like light evenings and point to fewer evening road accidents; critics say the change disturbs sleep for days. Most of Mexico stopped changing clocks in 2022.
asks: Why do some people want to stop changing clocks?

facts: Germany introduced daylight saving time in 1916, and Britain followed the same year.
London gets about 8 hours of daylight in late December and over 16 hours in late June.
